news.headline: 49ers lose Bosa, Evans and Samuel for Atlanta
news.detail: San Francisco ruled out DE Nick Bosa, WR Mike Evans and WR Deebo Samuel on the Oct 23 final report. Atlanta is also thin, with RB Brian Robinson and three defenders out and ten players questionable.

news.headline: Puka Nacua questionable with a calf injury
news.detail: Nacua did not practice Friday and is questionable. The Rams plan a pregame workout. Davante Adams is on injured reserve, so Stafford's receiver group is thin if Nacua sits. Cornerback Trent McDuffie is also questionable.

news.headline: Eagles short at receiver for Monday night
news.detail: DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks are tracking to miss, per Friday reports, and Jonathan Greenard is down. Saquon Barkley is expected to play. Dallas is likely without Kavontae Turpin and Dee Winters.

news.headline: Jalon Daniels the planned Bucs starter
news.detail: As of Oct 19-20, Tampa Bay planned to start Daniels, with Baker Mayfield's thumb being checked that week. The latest reporting found does not confirm Mayfield's status.

news.headline: Love cleared; Packers lose LB Zaire Franklin
news.detail: Jordan Love is off the final report with his back issue. Linebacker Zaire Franklin is out with a shin injury, and Edgerrin Cooper is on IR. Josh Jacobs is set to make his Packers debut. Detroit's report was nearly clean.

news.headline: Smith-Njigba healthy; Chiefs missing Rice and a tackle
news.detail: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is off the injury report this week. He caught 12 passes for 134 yards on Thursday night. Kansas City has WR Rashee Rice and right tackle Jaylon Moore out.

news.headline: Colts without Tyler Warren and Sauce Gardner
news.detail: Indianapolis ruled out TE Tyler Warren, CB Sauce Gardner and WR Anthony Gould. Minnesota is coming off its bye with only RB Jordan Mason questionable.

news.headline: McCarthy starts for Giants; both secondaries thin
news.detail: J.J. McCarthy is confirmed as the Giants starter. The Giants are without LB Tremaine Edmunds and CB Greg Newsome II. Houston has safeties Jalen Pitre and Reed Blankenship out. WR Tank Dell is questionable.

NFL.recap: The model went 6 of 14 on winners and 3-11 against the spread in the graded games, with an average miss of 8.2 points against Vegas's 6.2. Five games were missed by 10 points or more, all with the wrong winner, and the reviews mostly point to efficiency swings, plus turnovers for NYG-NO. Most likely winners are 3 of 5 and best value is 2 of 7, so fan-facing lists have run below the model's own chances. The latest result, CHI over NE, was another game where the model's pick differed from the Vegas favorite.

lessons.lesson: When the model picks a different winner than the Vegas favorite, it has lost so far.
lessons.evidence: 0 of 4 graded games (NYG over NO, ATL over CHI, PHI over CAR, NE over CHI) where the model's side was not the Vegas favorite. PHI over DAL on Monday would be a fifth.
lessons.test: On past seasons, take every game where the model's pick differs from the moneyline favorite. Compare its win rate and spread record with Vegas. Wait for 20+ games.

lessons.lesson: Large gaps between the model's total and Vegas's total have not paid off.
lessons.evidence: 0 of 4 graded games with a gap of 4.9 points or more (CHI 6.6, CAR 5.2, NE-CHI 5.0, BAL 4.9) won the over/under pick. Overall over/under is 5-9.
lessons.test: On past seasons, group games by size of the total gap (under 2, 2-4, over 4). Check hit rate per group. Needs 20+ games in the large-gap group.

lessons.lesson: Many big misses come from efficiency swings, which the model can't see before kickoff.
lessons.evidence: In 5 of the 8 games where the winner was wrong, the review names efficiency as a main reason. NO-NYG was turnovers, HOU-JAX had no clear reason, and NE-CHI was a close miss.
lessons.test: On past seasons, measure how often big spread misses (over 8 points) are driven by efficiency versus turnovers. Check whether the model's misses are larger than Vegas's overall.

lessons.lesson: Big-game player picks hit less often than the model's chances say.
lessons.evidence: 1 of 9 big-game picks hit, against 3.0 expected. The milestone picks went 7 of 9, against 6.8 expected.
lessons.test: On past seasons, compare predicted chance with actual hit rate for 300+ yard and similar long-shot props, in buckets of model chance. Needs 20+ picks.

lessons.lesson: Best-value picks against the sportsbook are underperforming.
lessons.evidence: 2 of 7 best-value picks hit this season, against 3.7 expected, at -3.18 units.
lessons.test: On past seasons, check hit rate of the model's top value picks by size of edge. Needs 20+ picks.

lessons.lesson: The model's margin errors are larger than Vegas's.
lessons.evidence: Average spread miss is 8.2 for the model against 6.2 for Vegas over 14 graded games, and the model is 3-11 against the spread.
lessons.test: On past seasons, compare the model's average absolute margin error with Vegas's, by week. Needs 20+ games, ideally a full season.

news.headline: Michigan State QB Milivojevic out at UCLA
news.detail: ESPN's Pete Thamel reported Saturday that Michigan State's starting quarterback will miss the game, and backup Cam Fancher is also out. Freshman Kayd Coffman is in line for his first start. The Spartans are missing their top four cornerbacks. UCLA is playing backup Ty Dieffenbach because Nico Iamaleava is out for the season.

news.headline: UCF QB Barnett reportedly not starting vs BYU
news.detail: ESPN reported on Oct 20 that UCF will start Keyone Jenkins again. Barnett is listed questionable, and UCF's coordinator said he has a fair chance, so it is not settled.

news.headline: Eastern Michigan QB Noah Kim questionable at Ohio
news.detail: Kim, who has 1,678 yards and 11 touchdowns, is listed questionable, and WR Nick Devereaux is out. Several Ohio defenders are also questionable.

news.headline: New Mexico on its third quarterback
news.detail: Backup James Laubstein tore a knee tendon and Jack Layne is out for the year, so freshman Toa Fa'avae starts. He went 5 of 10 for 59 yards with two interceptions last week. North Dakota State has injuries too, including safety Darius Givance.

news.headline: Colorado thin on offense at Oklahoma State
news.detail: Colorado has RB Micah Welch and receivers Perry and Scudero out. QB Isaac Wilson has been turnover-prone. Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker has thrown 300+ yards in five straight games.

news.headline: BC loses RB Dickens; Georgia Tech defense banged up
news.detail: Evan Dickens is out for the season. Georgia Tech is missing several defenders, including Noah Carter, Daiquan White and Savion Riley, and DT Tawfiq Thomas is doubtful.

news.headline: Kentucky down WR Nic Anderson and LB Sam Greene
news.detail: Both were ruled out for Vanderbilt. Vanderbilt is missing backup QB Blaze Berlowitz and several defenders, and is winless in the SEC.

College.recap: Week 8 games listed so far went 7 of 12 on winners, 6-6 against the spread and 8-4 on over/under. Season totals are 48 of 72 on winners, 37-31-2 against the spread and 39-31 on over/under, with an average miss of 11.3 against Vegas's 10.6. Of the 17 Week 7 games missed by 8+ points, the reviews name efficiency first in 12, turnovers in 3 and finishing drives in 2. Most likely winners are 6 of 6 and underdogs 3 of 5, while best-value is 2 of 7.

lessons.lesson: The 'model total 3+ above Vegas means the over hits' pattern may not hold up.
lessons.evidence: By my count in the Week 7-8 results listed, the over hit in 8 of 13 games where the model total was 3+ above Vegas (Week 7: 6 of 10; Week 8: 2 of 3). That is only slightly better than a coin flip, and the sample is under 20. No new games this run.
lessons.test: On past seasons, group games by model total minus Vegas total (0-3, 3-6, 6+) and check how often the over hits in each group. Need 20+ games per group.

lessons.lesson: Big misses mostly show up as efficiency gaps; turnovers and finishing drives come second.
lessons.evidence: Earlier set: efficiency was the top reason in 17 of 24 games missed by 8+. In the Week 7 list, 12 of 17 such games name efficiency first, 3 turnovers, 2 finishing drives. Efficiency is measured after the game, so it partly restates the miss. Week 8 results have no reviews.
lessons.test: On past seasons, check whether a team's success rate in prior games predicts the model's error next game. Also compare turnover margin and points per trip inside the 40 with the long-run average, to see if misses lean one way or are random.

lessons.lesson: When the model picks a different favorite than Vegas, early results are mixed, not bad.
lessons.evidence: 6 games with a different favorite: the model was right in 3 (Missouri State, Army, Marshall) and wrong in 3 (Cincinnati, Old Dominion, Rice over Tulsa). No new games this run. Sample is tiny.
lessons.test: On past seasons, list games where the model and Vegas disagree on the winner, then compare the model's win rate with Vegas's. Need 20+ games.

lessons.lesson: When the model has the favorite winning by 3+ more points than Vegas, the favorite has mostly not covered.
lessons.evidence: In the Week 7-8 results listed, 9 games fit (Utah, Fresno State, Houston, UCLA, NC State, Air Force, UConn, James Madison, Florida International). The favorite covered in 2 (UCLA over Wisconsin, UConn) and failed in 7. Today's BYU (gap 8.4), Troy (6.8), Ohio (9.0) and Kentucky (4.4) fit.
lessons.test: On past seasons, take games where the model's favorite margin is 3+ points above Vegas's and check the cover rate by size of gap (3-6, 6+). Need 20+ games per group.

lessons.lesson: The 'Best value against the sportsbook' list has been weak so far.
lessons.evidence: This season the list is 2 of 7 against 3.6 expected, at -3.18 units. Seven games is far too few to read, and the edges are thin (about 51% against 52.4% needed).
lessons.test: On past seasons, bucket the model's spread and total picks by edge size and compare hit rates with the 52.4% break-even. Need 20+ games per bucket.

lessons.lesson: Underdog picks have beaten the model's own chances so far.
lessons.evidence: 3 of 5 underdog picks hit, against 1.9 expected, at +4.59 units. Five picks is far too few to read.
lessons.test: On past seasons, compare predicted chance with actual win rate for the model's underdog picks, in buckets of model chance (under 35%, 35-45%). Needs 20+ picks.
